feature: Capture a window by clicking it
summary: During a region capture the window under the pointer now lights up with its app name and size, and one click captures exactly that window. Dragging a region works as before, and the drag box now shows its size too.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. The flag Capture a window by clicking it ships on. Have two or three app windows overlapping on the desktop before you start.

try.do: Press Shift Command 4 with the pointer already over an app window. The window should be lit and labelled before you move at all.
Slide the pointer across two overlapping windows. The highlight should jump to the front one under the pointer without lag.
Move onto the menu bar, then onto the Dock. Neither should light up; whatever window sits behind them does, or nothing.
Click once on a window. The capture toast should show that window at its exact bounds, and Edit should open it at the display's pixel scale.
Press Shift Command 4 again and drag out a region across a window. The drag box should show its size, and the result should be the region, not the window.
Press Shift Command 4 and press Escape. Then press Shift Command 4 and click on bare desktop. Both should cancel with nothing captured.
Press Shift Command 5 for a region recording, click a window, and stop the recording. The recording should cover that window's bounds.

evaluate: Is the app name plus size the right label, or do you want the window title as well?
Does the highlight land on the window you meant, or does a full-screen browser behind everything catch the pointer too often?
Is a click over bare desktop cancelling the right call, or should it capture the whole display?
Does the size pill on a drag help, or is it noise you would rather not have?
The capture stops at the window's bounds, no shadow and with the desktop showing through the rounded corners. Is that what you want from a window capture?
rough: The crop is a rectangle of the frozen screen, so a window's rounded corners keep whatever was behind them and no drop shadow is included. macOS's own window capture does the opposite by default. Filed as a follow-up.
The label says the app, not the window title, so two Safari windows read the same. The highlight itself shows which one. Filed as a follow-up.
Anything floating over the window in the frozen picture, such as a panel or a notification, is captured along with it, because the crop is the picture, not the window's own buffer.
A window straddling two displays captures only the part on the display you clicked in.

Verified on the loop's probe app with scripted mouse events on the real overlay: window pick, click, drag, desktop click and Escape all behaved. Live end-to-end with a real freeze is for you to try, since the loop has no Screen Recording grant.
